subject: Waverly Health — Trial environment onboarding & action grid
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.inference>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@waverlyhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya@waverlyhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Waverly Health — Trial environment onboarding & action grid

Hi Liam & Priya — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum on the trial: 

Summary of the ask
- Waverly wants to run a 4-week trial to validate: 1) latency under realistic traffic, 2) extraction accuracy on their clinical notes, and 3) multi-tenant security constraints.

Suggested success criteria (draft)
- 95th pct latency <= 250ms on hosted API for peak test load (70 concurrent flows).
- End-to-end entity extraction F1 >= 0.86 on your labeled evaluation set.
- No PII leakage per our QA sampling and audit logs during the trial window.

Environment options we discussed
1) Hosted (Redwood API) — fastest to start, no infra setup, data plane through Redwood (suitable for initial eval).
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPUs in our tenancy) — predictable throughput, isolated capacity, remote networking allowed for test harness.
3) VPC/private deployment — customer-managed networking and on-prem-like isolation (longer lead time; preferred for compliance-sensitive workloads).

Proposed path
- Start week 0 with Hosted API quick-run (3 business days) to sanity-check prompts and baseline metrics.
- Parallel: Ben to scope Dedicated sandbox resources if you want to ramp synthetic load tests week 1–3.
- If compliance gating requires, plan VPC kickoff week 3 with our infra team (longest path, depends on network access).

Owners & dates (proposal)
- Redwood: Neha (trial owner / PM), Ben (technical lead), Marissa (CS lead / onboarding).
- Waverly: Liam (product / throughput owner), Priya (security / compliance owner).
- Proposed start: 2026-01-20 (Hosted smoke test), Dedicated ramp 2026-01-22 — 02-12, VPC kickoff (if needed) 2026-02-09.

Ask from you
1) Confirm which environment(s) you want to include in the trial (Hosted only vs Hosted + Dedicated vs Start VPC).
2) Share a small sample of test corpus (anonymized) and the labeled eval set by EOD 01/16 so we can pre-compute token estimates.
3) Any compliance blockers we should know about (e.g., explicit disallow of third-party data plane).

I've attached a one-page success criteria sheet and a short network checklist that Ben will reference for Dedicated/VPC networking.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm environment choice.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — that recap is super helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- We're fine starting with Hosted to validate functional accuracy. If latency looks promising, we'd like to run Dedicated load tests in week 2.
- We can provide an anonymized sample set and the labeled eval by Friday 01/16 — Priya will send that.
- Compliance: neutral on data plane for the trial, but will escalate if any PII concerns appear; Priya will own that.

Couple of quick technical Qs for Ben:
- What token-cost should we plan for for 50k tokens/day during load tests?
- For Dedicated sandbox, can we reserve GPUs with pre-warmed KV cache for repeated runs?

Liam

On Wed, Jan 14, 2026 at 5:10 PM Liam O'Connor <liam@waverlyhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Neha — that recap is super helpful. Quick answers from our side:
> 
> - We're fine starting with Hosted to validate functional accuracy. If latency looks promising, we'd like to run Dedicated load tests in week 2.

Thanks Liam — quick technical notes:

1) Token cost estimate
- For planning, 50k tokens/day for our generator/encoder mix typically maps to ~1.2 GPU-hours/day on a mid-range instance in Dedicated; that converts to our trial estimate of ~36 GPU-hours/week. I'll put exact per-token cost in the HubSpot deck.

2) KV cache / pre-warm
- We can pre-warm KV caches for Dedicated sandbox runs (this reduces cold-start latency significantly). For repeated runs it's best to schedule warm-up requests ~30 minutes prior. We also support snapshotting a model KV state for faster resume.

3) Networking & firewall
- If you choose Dedicated or VPC, see attached network checklist. For VPC we'll need a temporary peering/VPN or whitelisted IP ranges and an expected egress pattern for audit.

I'll put together a simple cost & infra worksheet (numbers) and drop it into the Drive link Neha referenced.

Ben Carter
Technical Solutions, Redwood Inference
